subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>: tall and deeply sinuous, waist-length neon-green hair breaking into flying strands, pale mint-white armored headgear with two swept antenna fins and side ear pods, light-green eyes and a small hard mouth; her body is wrapped in a dark aubergine sleeveless bodysuit traced with thin neon-green piping, high-cut hip openings and a mint-edged V neckline, with mint armored heeled boots. Both forearms carry heavy mechanical weapon rigs — forest-green and gunmetal housings with exposed barrels, hydraulic rods, cable bundles and drum magazines. <Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1]: a full-body studio frame against a pale background, and it supplies her identity, costume, silhouette and weapon rigs.
<Subject 2> is the woman in <Picture 2>: petite and curvy, light-green hair gathered in a high twin-tail cluster with one thin antenna strand, sharp green eyes, a black armored bodysuit with a pink shoulder guard and a pink-and-green chest panel, black shorts on a pink belt with green trim and a thigh strap over black thigh-high stockings, pink-and-black shoulder pods studded with colored optic lenses, and two massive arm cannons of black and pink blocks with a glowing blue emitter disc; black heeled boots with pink toes. <Picture 2> supplies her identity and costume design only.

summary:
[reference generation + keyframe completion] An eight-second pursuit in a ruined megacity where <Subject 1> sprints away while her torso twists back and her arm rigs fire behind her at <Subject 2>, who hunts her through the same streets; the shot begins from <Picture 1>. Both women stay feverish, defiant and impossible to tame.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - her identity, neon-green hair, mint headgear, aubergine piping bodysuit and both heavy arm rigs are retained.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the first frame reproduces the studio full-body framing, costume lines and weapon rigs, then breaks into motion.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - her identity, twin-tail green hair, black-and-pink bodysuit and shorts, shoulder pods, thigh-highs and twin arm cannons are retained.

detailed_description:
Hand-drawn 2D anime in the MAPPA feature-film manner: fine cel linework, flat two-tone shadow, painted city backgrounds with deep aerial perspective and layered haze, 4K cinema finish with light grain. Bodies stay pliant and alive — flesh compresses and ripples under every impact, and dozens of independent armor plates, pistons, cables and pods ride on their own joints. The camera behaves like a free aerial operator with a handheld breathing sway, rising and falling and covering long distances, while the frame contains only the two women, the ruined architecture and the flying debris. Every object keeps a continuous physical history: gear, props and rubble enter and leave the frame only behind solid cover, and bodies, weapons and debris hold solid contact and clean occlusion.
The first frame begins an eight-second continuous performance, with no preliminary recap, title card or neutral waiting pose. Every shot timestamp is measured from decoded-frame zero; phase timing inside each shot is measured from that shot entry.
[Shot 1: 00:00.000 - 00:02.400 | Backward Barrage At Full Sprint]
Start state: At 00:00.000 the frame is <Picture 1> exactly, weight already loaded on the back foot, chin low, one green eye cutting up at the lens. From 00:00.000 to 00:02.400 she explodes forward down a rain-slick avenue of collapsed towers, spine twisted so her chest faces camera-left while the right arm rig swings behind her and both barrels track back on <Subject 2>, spitting burst-fire with every stride. The camera drops behind her shoulder and glides low, bobbing vertically, then swoops up over a stalled bus and banks hard as she cuts a corner around a fallen billboard, plants one boot on buckled steel and vaults, hair and hip swaying through the whip of the turn.
[Shot 2: 00:02.400 - 00:05.800 | Lost Trail, Long Pivot]
At 00:02.400 the shot cuts to <Subject 2> sprinting the same avenue in pursuit, framed over her shoulder; the camera pans hard left and snaps straight back to her line of sight, hunting, her head whipping after the sound. Deep in the frame <Subject 1> drops out of the sprint under a collapsed overpass slab, sliding on her hip into cover, then braces the rig on the concrete and slaps a fresh drum home against her thigh. <Subject 2> slaps her side flat to a concrete corner, shoulder pods swiveling and locking, and punches a fresh drum into her cannon feed. The camera rockets forward up the street in one long travel, rotating as it flies, and settles behind <Subject 1> in a tumbling first-person spin that straightens out as she bursts into long strides, snaps a side roll over the asphalt and comes up planted; a medium shot finds her leaning one eye past the slab edge, ribs heaving.
[Shot 3: 00:05.800 - 00:08.000 | POV Lock-On And Launch]
At 00:05.800 the view snaps into <Subject 1>'s first-person sightline, tunnel-wide with heavy handheld roll, and finds <Subject 2> straightening from the wall down the avenue. Her arm rigs swing up and lock; at 00:06.800 the camera punches back to a profile medium as she shoulders the weight, brace plates swinging open, and fires, the flash whitening one frame edge and lifting a sheet of dust. Down the street <Subject 2> throws herself off the wall into the air, already tucking into a forward somersault with both cannons rising as the segment ends.

overall_soundscape:
Wet bootfalls, servo whine and hydraulic hiss, the flat crack of heavy rounds, rubble skittering, both women breathing hard through clenched teeth; low ruined-city ambience underneath.

## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.
